A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same latent-learning study. Their text, equations, figures, Table 1, and Appendices A–C are available and support reliable comparison, including material relocated through pagination changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-training and evaluation results on codebooks, simple reversals, semantic structure, and gridworld navigation, including supplemental ablations in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their results in Section 6 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B retain the same transformer and IMPALA training procedures, reconstruction objectives, oracle retrieval, and treatment of retrieved context. No algorithm or model component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same codebook, reversal, semantic-structure, and gridworld tasks, including both semantic-cue conditions and pixel-based RL and ASCII-based behavioral cloning.

E2.justification: The baseline, oracle-retrieval, and ablation comparator sets remain unchanged in Figures 3–11. Newly cited bidirectional models and tool-use systems are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Reported splits, sample counts, metrics, model sizes, retrieval settings, and Table 1 hyperparameters are retained. The additional tree-construction description in Section 4.3 documents an existing condition without establishing that its evaluation protocol changed.

E4.justification: Both retain the semantic-cue comparison, within-experience ICL ablations, and Appendix C controls for batch size, irrelevant retrieval, training-map count, and BC sequence length. No new analytical experiment is reported.

E5.justification: Figures 3–4 retain 95% confidence intervals across four runs. Figure 6 retains binomial intervals for BC and bootstrap intervals across three RL runs. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The result graphics and reported findings in Figures 3–11 are unchanged, including the approximately 12% reversal and 6% codebook latent-test performance without ICL in Figure 7. No result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Section 3 explicitly adds causal reconstruction to its assumptions and restricts the reversal-without-context prediction to causal language models. The input/task mapping, non-injectivity discussion, and four prediction cases otherwise remain, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims about latent-learning failures, complementary oracle retrieval, and the importance of ICL remain. The hippocampal and replay interpretation newly highlighted in the abstract and contribution list was already developed in v2's Discussion.

C2.justification: New footnote 2 explains that bidirectional prediction can avoid reversal failure and that explicit versus latent information depends on architecture and objective. Sections 2.3 and 7 refine the interpretation of parametric generalization and describe offline augmentation as applying a similar retrieval-based computation ahead of time.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 newly specifies that the reduced-cue semantic dataset uses a wider, shallower tree with heavier branching near the top. This supplements the existing distractor-selection description; Appendix B's implementation details and access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 expands the existing discussion of parametric generalization with classic connectionist and newer compositional-learning references. Further citations address replay, memory organization, tool use, and bidirectional reversal behavior; Murty et al. (2023) is removed. The central research positioning remains.

P1.justification: v3 expands the introductory reversal example, adds Section 2.3, revises the Section 3 heading, and locally rewrites background and discussion passages. Terminology shifts toward similarity-based generalization and experiences or episodes. The overall section order and appendices remain.

P2.justification: Figure 1's schematic panels and wording are revised, and Figure 5's panel headings and caption adopt similarity-based terminology. Text and figure placement shift with reflow, but all eleven figures and Table 1 are retained without substantial display restructuring.

improvement.justification: v3 improves conceptual precision through Section 2.3's clearer distinction between latent learning and established parametric generalization, and footnote 2's explicit causal-model qualification. Section 4.3 also improves dataset documentation. These refinements make the retained evidence easier to interpret, while the experiments and the acknowledged practical difficulty of retrieving relevant memories remain unchanged.
